expectations.evidence: Line 37 explicitly lists: 'NATO SECRET (fourth tier in NATO UNCLASSIFIED / NATO RESTRICTED / NATO CONFIDENTIAL / NATO SECRET / COSMIC TOP SECRET)'
Line 45: 'Authority: NSM (Nasjonal Sikkerhetsmyndighet / National Security Authority)' under the Norway section
Line 60: 'Authority: BSI (Bundesamt fur Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik) for IT security; BMVg (Federal Ministry of Defence) for military classification'
Line 53: 'Authority: CFCS (Center for Cybersikkerhed)' under the Denmark section

Section 7.1 defines four physically isolated domains: NATO SECRET shared domain plus three national enclaves (NOR HEMMELIG, DNK HEMMELIGT, DEU GEHEIM). Line 23: 'each nation requires a segregated enclave for nationally-classified data...that is accessible only to that nation's cleared personnel.' NATO SECRET is explicitly the shared tier.

Line 40: 'NATO-approved cryptographic products only for NATO SECRET data in transit and at rest'. Line 432 details: 'AES-256 (NATO-approved implementation)' for data at rest, 'TLS 1.3 with NATO-approved cipher suites; Type 1 for WAN' for transit.

Section 8 (Cross-Domain Solutions) extensively covers CDS architecture with hardware guards, content inspection, release procedures, and approval workflows. Line 451: 'Direct transfers between national enclaves are not permitted. All inter-nation sharing goes through the NATO SECRET shared domain.' Lines 501-502 detail release authority requirements for each direction.

Section 2.2 'Bilateral and Multilateral Security Agreements' lists required agreements: General Security Agreement (GSA) between all three pairs, Programme Security Instruction (PSI), CIS Security MoU, accreditation agreement, and TEMPEST agreement.

Lines 410-417 define clearance requirements per domain: NATO SECRET clearance for shared domain (all nations), national clearance for national enclaves (restricted to that nation only). Line 629 shows Infrastructure Lead requires 'NATO SECRET + all national'. National enclaves explicitly restricted to that nation's personnel only (NOR only, DNK only, DEU only), meaning access to another nation's data requires specific authorization.

Line 107: 'Cable routing must enforce red/black separation -- classified (red) and unclassified (black) signals must never share conduits.' Also extensive TEMPEST coverage: NATO SDIP-27 Zone A/B compliance, TEMPEST-rated equipment, emanation leakage prevention.

Line 39: 'Accreditation authority: NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA), in coordination with the host nation's NSA and participating nations' NSAs.' Line 81: 'NATO SECRET shared domain | NCIA + NSM (host nation lead)' in the accreditation table.

Section 3.1 details LIST-X equivalent facility requirements: controlled access area with 24/7 guard force, intrusion detection, CCTV, multi-factor access control with mantrap entry, visitor escort, internal zoning per security domain, and NSM conducts physical and IT security inspections (line 47).
